SBC correctly draws the latent from the known generating prior, then the observation and independent posterior draws, and tests that same latent. With31 posterior draws the randomized rank belongs to0..31; the newly explicit sum(rank_i)/(31*N) has mean1/2 under a correct continuous posterior, and each histogram bin is count/N with target1/32. The earlier normalization ambiguity is resolved. Tie uniforms remain explicitly drawn in the stream even though ties have probability zero mathematically. The population residual variance,95-percent central boundary and every conjunctive threshold are fixed. This interpretation follows the known-joint rank validation boundary in Talts et al., Validating Bayesian Inference Algorithms with Simulation-Based Calibration, https://arxiv.org/html/1804.06788v2; it checks implementation within the assumed joint and is not empirical coverage or validation of that generating law.

I independently derived the Gaussian negative controls without simulation. When the assumed observation noise is2R, standardized residual variance is(4R+1/2)/(2*(1/2+2R)), yielding2/3 inA and3/4 inB. Their exact central95-percent coverages are approximately0.983625 and0.976375, each more than0.015 from0.95, so the locked variance/coverage countercontrols are nonvacuous. Wrong prior means shift residual means to-sqrt(2/5) and-sqrt(2/3), agreeing with the protocol. The nonstationary-mean transformation preserves covariance and the unchanged transition while requiring the actual shifted predictive mean; substituting stationary mean gives an observable residual bias. These exact target checks do not assert power1 or guarantee the unseen Monte Carlo results.

The new fixed-latent consistency scope is mathematically correct. For one latent Z~Gaussian(c,1/2) measured repeatedly with independent noiseR>0 and no intervening transition, conjugacy gives P_n=R/(2R+n) and m_n=(2R*c+sumY_j)/(2R+n). The posterior error under the actual joint has MSE R*(2R+n)/(2R+n)^2=P_n. Markov's inequality then bounds Pr(|m_n-Z|>=epsilon) by P_n/epsilon^2, which tends to0 for every epsilon>0. At n0 the formulas return the original prior; deterministic prefixes through n16 need no new draws. This proves the intended convergence-in-probability statement under the declared joint only. It neither gives a pointwise-for-every-truth guarantee nor an almost-sure infinite-process theorem, hidden-state identification, parameter consistency or changing-state filtering concentration.

I checked the intervention and information formulas relevant to the claimed interpretation. A constant active-coordinate pushforward preserves the other joint marginal while yielding covariance1/56 and variances15/56 conditional on sensory; the stationary conditional blanket does not transfer. The EFE preference Gaussian(0,1/2) gives squared terminal risk plus(1/2)log(pi) minus action-common Gaussian mutual information; mean1/preference-center1 strictly reverses the declared risk ordering. Pointwise convexity yields the stated finite-horizon moment bound with unchanged hidden-mode total second moment2/3, without infinite-horizon stability. The uncontrolled three-time AR covariance gives path KL2*(1-exp(-1)), while repeated time points give different forward/reversed supports and require native infinite KL. Equal path laws with different stated energy-per-nat assignments are a constitutive nonidentification witness, not measured heat.
